answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity carry reputation that is expensive to rebuild. An agent earns trust only by completing verifiable work, like quartz growing layer by layer, so a fresh fake identity starts with nothing. A reputation graph acts as a nebula of attestations: peers vouch for agents they have actually transacted with, and newcomers vouching only for each other look suspicious. Finally, a costly entry stake locked for months, like a reef that takes years to form, makes spawning thousands of identities uneconomic.
